title: What To Do in the First 24 Hours After a Car Accident
metaDescription: A calm, step-by-step checklist for safety, medical care, documentation, and talking with insurers after a car crash. Educational only—not legal advice.
excerpt: A calm, step-by-step checklist for safety, medical care, documentation, and talking with insurers.

sections.heading: Start with safety
paragraphs: The first day after a crash often feels chaotic. Your priority is safety, then health, then documentation.
If anyone may be injured, call 911. Move vehicles only when it is safe and required by local rules.
list: Turn on hazard lights and set flares if available
Check yourself and passengers before assessing vehicles
Stay out of traffic lanes when possible

sections.heading: Document and exchange information
paragraphs: Exchange insurance and contact information. Photograph the scene, vehicles, plates, and any visible injuries.
Collect witness names and phone numbers. Note weather, lighting, and road conditions.

sections.heading: Medical care and insurance
paragraphs: Seek medical care promptly—even mild symptoms can worsen. Keep every bill and visit note.
Notify your insurer with basic facts. You may wish to speak with a licensed attorney before giving a recorded statement.

faq.question: Should I admit fault at the scene?
faq.answer: Stick to facts when speaking with officers and other drivers. Fault is often determined later with evidence.

faq.question: Do I have to give a recorded statement right away?
faq.answer: Requirements vary. Many people consult a licensed attorney before recorded statements. This article is general education only.
